about: Creatures: how many and how they grow, move, notice, nap, guard and fight.

combatWaiting.what: Waiting movement favours room beyond a set invitation reach (inviteReach: the default bag's old range, not the letters' live one) while allowing deliberate close passes.
combatWaiting.notes: reachScale multiplies dash distance times charges plus inviteReach, the default invitation range that set the room (33 m, held there when the letters got 42 m, so they reach the circling animals; neither buffs nor a bag like the Clutch move it); areaGrowth adds a fraction of area radius beyond that reference, without clamping small areas. passPower concentrates the smooth close-pass pulse; passDepth sets how far that pulse relaxes the outward preference. Species routes, speed and turning remain in the pack profiles.

decisions.quote: creatures should be moving most of the time, and tend to be outside of her (default bag) range if they're not attacking
it feels like animals move faster than invitations so it's hard to land a hit. And ranges feel small
decisions.rest: the letters' speed and range raised while holding the animals' waiting distance where it was: inviteReach 33, the old invite range, so the reference stays (30 + 33) x 0.8 = 50.4 m

teamRounds.what: A big pack's attacks come round faster and keep coming: shorter rounds past `reference` animals, attackers picked `ahead` rounds early, and waiting rings of `ring`.
teamRounds.notes: The round's scale is (reference / size) ^ strength, at least floor, and 1 at or under reference (rules/combat/teams.ts roundScale). With reference 20, strength 0.5 (inverse square root) and floor 0.4: 20 animals 5 s rounds as before; 64, 2.8 s; 128, 2 s (the floor). The attack window shrinks the same only down to `window` of it (1 by default: kept at 3 s). The lull's least rest (its kinds' rhythm lull) shrinks the same, as it otherwise held the round at about 7 s; the tell before a combo is never shortened. Her dodge token (dodge.a.tokens, swarmTokens) is unchanged: still one creature winding up or striking at her at once. `ahead`: a team past `reference` keeps its attackers picked this many rounds ahead (the same seeded draw each round would make; 0 off), and those picked leave the waiting ring when, at their own pace, they'd only just reach their ready distance (their next action's reach) as their round's window opens, instead of starting their run then; the rest keep to the waiting ring (rules/combat/teams.ts, rules/combat.ts movingGoal). `ring`: past this many (20), the team waits in rings of this many, the inner one this round's attackers and the coming rounds' picks first, each further ring RANK_GAP (1.5) of its own body gaps out, each ring's gap its own members' bodies and clearance shared out (rules/combat.ts movingGoal, rules/combatSpacing.ts); 0 one ring of all, as before. `window`: the least share of the 3 s attack window a big team keeps, 1 by default (the window never shortened; Ed, 2026-11-04, "Resolve the attack rate limit for 128": a shortened window let barely one strike through her dodge token a round). Defaults ahead 3, ring 20, window 1 (Ed asked why not 3 rounds ahead: it measured better at 128).

decisions.quote: how about we have the attack round length decrease gradually as the pack gets larger
can we decide the roles in advance and have them move in sooner, in time for their attack?
Resolve the attack rate limit for 128, then publish 1782.

difficulty.what: How hard the creatures are: faster in a fight, further with their ranged attacks, and adults stronger.

decisions.quote: Animals +20% speed, ranged attacks have +20% range, adults are stronger.

difficulty.notes: Ed, 2026-11-03: "the game is much too easy". The pause page's Difficulty sliders set them live. All three at 1: as before.

difficulty.creatureSpeed.what: every creature's movement speed in a fight times this: its run, its sprint closing in and its chase at her, a heavy's top speed, charges, swoops, a legend's charge, a besieger's march (not her, not its shots, lunges, leaps or hops' timing, nor a creature's roaming or leash pace).

difficulty.rangedRange.what: every ranged attack's reach times this, at anything: a shot, a lob or a beam (its cast's range, its bolt's life and a beam's length), never a melee one or a pulse round itself.
difficulty.rangedRange.notes: On top of dodge.b.range at her. Legends' own throws and beams as they were.

difficulty.adultStrength.what: an adult's health (a full 💌 ring's worth of blows) and damage in a fight times this, hers and the wild's alike; its evolving cost and the swarm builder's estimates as they were.

fight.what: The scale and speed fights are played at, with creatures running at about her speed.

decisions.quote: the animals don't move around enough when attacking and defending
Charging creatures can easily be evaded by just walking away from them. They should jump far enough or charge far enough that this doesn't work

fight.notes: The fight's scale and speed [1]: fights are drawn and played at the ground camera's scale, creatures running at about the witch's speed and their patterns about 50 m across. Every leap: reach times how far off it leaps from, a pounce (the lynx's) landing through metres past its target (a slam, the toad's, still onto it); Walking away is no escape [2]: charge.chase, a charge runs at least that many times her ground speed and on until it has caught up with her walking straight down its lane (its own time if longer), so stepping out of the lane at its tell, a blink sideways or the treetops get her clear, walking doesn't (0: off); leap.lead, a leap comes down where she'll be when it lands, as she's going at take-off (that share of it; 0: where she was).

fight.scale.what: every length in a fight times this (attack ranges, lunges, area radii, beam widths, knockback, the packs' patterns and spacing, pursuit and guard reach, aggro).

fight.speed.what: every fight speed times this (running, charging, lunging, shots).

fight.momentum.what: How heavily creatures in a fight speed up, brake and turn.

decisions.quote: they should have more momentum

fight.momentum.notes: how heavily creatures in a fight change speed and turn: their accelerations, braking and turn rates divided by it (2: twice as heavy). Try ?fightScale= and ?fightSpeed=, or change them live on the pause page (Esc): its Debug knobs sliders, or [ and ] for scale; and ' for speed,, and. for momentum.

fight.charge.what: every species' charge (movement.json) scaled: reach its run's time and overshoot past its target, turn its turn rate (lower: wider arcs), brake how hard it slows (lower: more momentum).

decisions.rest: round 13: 'charging and jumping creatures should charge or jump much further... damaging whenever they're touched while in attack mode... much more momentum, travelling in wide arcs'

fight.charge.contact.what: it hurts every foe it touches on the way, once each (her grace making one charge one hit). a pounce hurts whoever it touches in the air.

fight.charge.miss.what: a charge that struck nothing stands winded that many seconds after (stars round its head), an opening for her 💌s [1].

decisions.quote: We want to reward skilful use of blink and accurate invitation aiming

creatureMomentum.what: Creatures chasing her carry momentum on their run-in and wind-up, so she can dodge past them.

decisions.quote: most animals don't have enough momentum and can turn too sharply, or alternatively track the witch too quickly and accurately ... less worth dodging

quote: all these as options, which we can tweak later
prediction is ok, but it should mostly be for telegraphed attacks
each creature can have different amounts of each
decisions.rest: rules/momentum.ts

creatureMomentum.notes: Creature momentum [1][2], chasing the witch only (fights between creatures, legends and marchers as before): on its run-in and its wind-up (a pack's tell and combo too), never its committed lunge, which goes where the wind-up aimed, reaching up to a quarter again its usual length if the run-in left it short [3], so a strike that starts stays reliable. The pause page's sliders (Creature momentum) are global: turn, delay and strikeLead multiply every species' values, chaseLead adds seconds to every species' own; on false: as before.

creatureMomentum.turn.what: its heading swings at most turn / (1 + its speed / k) degrees a second (also divided by fight.momentum), slowing to turn tighter when she's far off its heading, so a fast one sidestepped overshoots in an arc.

creatureMomentum.delay.what: it steers for where she was that many seconds ago (a short trail of her places), so a sidestep or blink fools it a moment.

creatureMomentum.chaseLead.what: seconds of her velocity it leads her by when just chasing (0: none).

creatureMomentum.strikeLead.what: times the lead its telegraphed attacks take (a melee wind-up's tracking, dodge.a.lead; a charge's lane, dodge.b.chargeLead; a leap, fight.leap.lead; a swoop's dive; shots and lobs, dodge.b.lead).

creatureMomentum.classes.what: each class's values (heavy: dodge.a.heavy's species; light: those with the nimble or swarm trait; normal: everyone else), and a species may set its own in its folder (art/creatures/<id>/creature.js movement.momentum).

attackFx.what: How attacks feel on screen: attackers crouch and lunge, hits squash their target, and hard knock-backs send it tumbling.

decisions.quote: make creature attack visuals better
decisions.rest: render/attackFeel.ts

attackFx.notes: How attacks feel on screen [1], a party not a fight: windupSquash, how low and wide an attacker crouches as its wind-up nears the blow (at most windupMax seconds of it shown); lungeStretch, how far it stretches out in its lunge; squash, how flat a hit squashes the one it hits, springing back past its shape over squashSecs seconds; a knock-back thrown faster than tumbleKnock m/s tumbles: up tumbleHeight metres (at most 1.5 times that for the hardest) for tumbleSecs, over on its back from turnFrom to turnTo of the way (one slow beat, never a strobe), landing with a squash. Squash and stretch go in whole art pixels.

attackFx.legendFlash.what: how much bigger and longer a legend's blow flashes than anyone's (its flash 1 + 2 × legendFlash times; 0.5, twice: Ed's decisions panel, config/decisions.json).

attackFx.visibility.what: How easy the creatures' spells are to see: their size, opacity, glow, how long they last, how thick their lingering zones are and how strong the marks they leave on the ground (1, 0, 1, 1, 0.25 and 0.12 draw them as before 3 November).

decisions.quote: Let's dial up current creature spell effects a lot so they're easier to see. Larger, extra Bloom. Don't bring back the flash and rings yet.
decisions.rest: size 1.75, opacity 0.9, bloom 2, duration 1.5, zoneDensity 0.5, groundMark 0.45; the pause page's Creature spells sliders (config/decisions)

attackFx.visibility.notes: size: every creature spell's size times this (bolts and lobs, their trails, hits, ground marks, beams' width, status icons, pack specials; a quake's or pulse's ground spreads a little past its true reach, 40% of the extra). opacity: how far each spell's own opacity is raised toward solid (0: as it was; 1: all solid), so a themed shot's 0.45 goes to 0.95 and a beam's 0.65 to 0.97. bloom: its halo, the halo seen through the crowns, its glow on the ground and the extra glow round bolts, hits, beams and zones, times their own (lights by half as much, at most 1.5 times). duration: hits, marks, quakes and trails last this many times as long. zoneDensity: the share of a lingering zone's tiles drawn (0.25 was every fourth; 1 every one). groundMark: how opaque a hit's mark on the ground starts (it was 0.12).

attackFx.glow.what: How the creatures' spells glow: a bright core the bloom picks up, a dithered pixel halo round it, a pool of its light on the ground under it, and a real light for the brightest few nearest her (core, halo, pool and light 0 draw them as before 9 November; ?spellglow=0 does too, to compare).

decisions.quote: The animal magic effects need to glow.
decisions.rest: core 1, halo 1, pool 1, lights 5, light 1; the look is the magic brief's (docs/backlog/magic-effects.md §5, Ed 2026-10-28: "Pixel cores and dithered pixel halos, with a small smooth bloom over the top"; effect lights allowed, capped at about six)

attackFx.glow.notes: core: how bright the glowing core added over each spell's own is, in its element's bright colour (a party animal's: its neon), enough to cross the bloom's threshold, so the bloom gives it a small smooth glow (0 none). halo: the dithered halo round bolts, hits and beams, in three art-pixel steps fading out (0 none). pool: its light's pool on the ground under every spell in flight (smaller and fainter the higher it flies, so the lit spot shows its height), at its hits and across lingering zones and quakes (0 none). lights: at most this many spells light the world around them at once (the strongest nearest her first, sharing the effects' six slots, config/fx/intensity.json lightCap, within the light budget; easing in and out, the world's farthest lights making room the same way, so none pops); 0 none. light: those lights' strength (1 as the magic layers' own). Reduce flashing (the Settings page) halves core, halo, pool and light; nothing in the glow flickers.

attackFx.magicGlow.what: How her own magic glows, with the same pieces as the creatures' spells: a bright core the bloom picks up, a dithered pixel halo round it, a pool of its light on the ground under it, and a real light where it earns one (all four at 0 draw her magic as before 13 November; ?magicglow=0 does too, to compare).

decisions.quote: extend
decisions.rest: asked whether to extend the creatures' glow (2026-11-09: "The animal magic effects need to glow.") to her own magic, which #1928 had left with its own look; core 1, halo 1, pool 1, light 1; the look is still the magic brief's (Ed, 2026-10-28: "Pixel cores and dithered pixel halos, with a small smooth bloom over the top")

attackFx.magicGlow.notes: What glows: the party start's analyser ring at her decks (each bar's tip a core in the bar's colour with its halo and a pool on the floor, and one light over the decks); her blink (where she left, where she lands, and a streak of light with its pool along the way); the ley line's spark (core, halo, pool, light); the soundsystem spell's eruption, vortex and dome and a cleared challenge's; and pools on the ground under her flight trail (in the trail's colour, smaller and fainter the higher she flies), under party witches' swoops, placed sigils and the ring's dots (config/fx/native.json glow: no core where one would cover her or a sigil's glyph). core: how bright the glowing cores are (0 none). halo: the dithered halo round them (0 none). pool: the pools on the ground (0 none). light: her magic's real lights' strength (1 as before; 0 none). Lights: her magic shares the effects' six slots with the creatures' spells; her cast magic (the blink, the party start, the ley line's spark) takes the first two when both want slots, the creatures' spells keep at least four (attackFx.glow.lights caps them at five), and every light still eases in and out with the world's farthest lights making room, so none pops. Reduce flashing (the Settings page) halves core, halo, pool and light; nothing in the glow flickers.

combat.what: How creatures fight: who goes for whom, how fast they run and chase, and how much a soundsystem and home's speakers can take.

decisions.quote: Animals seem to walk very slowly when they're going towards soundsystems they plan to attack
decisions.rest: it was its walk times marchMult, under 1 m/s, and marchOnRun 5 m/s marching on

decisions.quote: seem to struggle to damage soundsystems
decisions.rest: some; a charge struck once a run, a swoop once a dive
from 4000: shorter games, falls that cascade, and you must stop a swarm before it arrives

decisions.quote: home as 12 speakers at 500 hp each
decisions.rest: rules/speakers.ts

combat.notes: Combat (Stage 4; the attacks themselves are data in config/combat.json; lengths and speeds at the fight's scale: see fight). Wild creatures attack party animals of other kinds within aggro metres. They go for the witch on the ground as soon as she's in their area or within their attack's range [1], and let her go when she rises to the treetops, or once she's out of their area, out of their range and at least witchLose metres away; then they walk back to their spot. The one she's inviting holds its fire on her (its friends don't). Party animals following her take on what attacks her or her party; parked ones (at a sigil) guard within guard.radius of it. Babies are never attacked, by either side. Marching on a soundsystem, its own area's or marching on after a fall, a creature moves at marchShare of its top (fight) speed: its movement profile's, else fightRun, a legend legendRun [2]. Against a soundsystem or speaker, charging kinds don't charge and swoopers don't swoop: they land and use their ordinary attack [3]. A beaten creature, wild or party, runs off the map at fleeMult times its speed and is gone for good [4]; a party animal is lost for the run. A soundsystem has soundsystemHealth, passive, and is hit within soundsystemRadius metres: sieges should outlast the wave gap. A soundsystem has 500 [5]. Home is its ring of speakers [6], each a soundsystem of speakerHealth, hit within speakerRadius metres, the besiegers going for the nearest standing one; home falls when every one has (its old homeHealth 8000 and homeRadius 9 gone).

combat.packs.shadow.what: A pack member hiding in its lull (in the trees, underground, under water, in the branches, or scattered) is drawn as a shadow of itself, not left out.

decisions.quote: 'hiding' maybe should look like the animal becoming a shadow (dark and transparent), rather than teleporting

combat.packs.shadow.notes: Hiding looks like a shadow [1]: while it's hidden (and can't be hit) it's drawn as its own sprite darkened by shade (0 its own colours, 1 black) at opacity, running round to where it comes back, fading from solid to shadow over fade seconds as it hides and back as it comes out (render/view/creatures.ts).

combat.packs.shadow.shade.what: How dark: 0 its own colours, 1 black.

combat.packs.shadow.opacity.what: How opaque the shadow is (0 invisible, 1 solid).

combat.packs.shadow.fade.what: Seconds to turn from solid to shadow as it hides, and back as it comes out.

combat.packs.what: Pack kinds fight in combos (the nearest lunges, the ranged fire where she'd dodge, one behind her throws its special) and fall back between them.

decisions.rest: docs/backlog/combat.md, build step 1

decisions.quote: Turn pack combat on by default

combat.packs.notes: pack combat [1], on by default [2] and on the pause page to turn off for testing: on, packs of config/packs.json's kinds (home's ten and Phase 1's eleven) fight in combos (the nearest lunges, the ones at range fire where a dodge would go, the one behind her throws the special), fall back by their kind's retreat between combos, and her own pack combos without retreating.

combat.aggro.what: wild creatures go for party animals within this, and for the witch anywhere in their area.

combat.leaveArea.what: How far past its area's edge a wild creature chases another creature, or comes out after her across its edge, before going home; once it's after her it follows her anywhere on the ground until she takes off.

decisions.rest: round 13: 30; it was 10

combat.leaveArea.notes: Since Ed's 31 Oct playtest a wild creature after her follows her anywhere on the ground until she takes off (rules/combat/targeting.ts); this band now bounds only creature-against-creature chases and coming out after her across its edge. Before: a wild one chasing the witch gives up once she's this far past its area's edge, and turns back home (besiegers keep witchLose: they give up once she's out of their area, out of range and this far off). a wild creature chases her (or her party) up to this many metres past its area's edge [2]; beyond it, or once she rises, it gives up and retreats into its area at its own pace, roaming again once it's in and within retreatHome metres of home, taking up a fight on the way only with someone back in its area (no flip-flopping at the edge). Besiegers march as before; happy and leashed ones aren't affected.

combat.pursuit.what: how far from her (or its sigil, guarding) a party animal chases a foe before giving up.

combat.pursuitRun.what: how fast it closes in while over 30 m off (so an area's creatures are onto her in a few seconds when she lands in it).

combat.fightRun.what: how fast a creature runs in a fight (m/s), when its movement profile doesn't say (movement.json speed).

combat.reaction.what: seconds before a creature that has just noticed something goes for it.

combat.shake.what: how hard a legend's quake shakes the screen (0 none).

combat.daze.what: seconds a wild creature knocked down in a fight lies stunned (nothing attacks it, it attacks nothing, she can still invite it; it counts as present for its legend, and no siege takes it) before it runs off home [1].

decisions.quote: the length of the stun of wild creatures that are downed in combat, before they run away, should be 20 seconds
decisions.rest: round 13; it was 8, states.json's daze

combat.defendRadius.what: her animals following her within this many metres of her go first for anything attacking her, spread over her attackers; farther off, following her, one fights back only at what's on it itself (and parked, guarding or travelling ones carry on as they were): never pulled across to her fight.

decisions.quote: just ones that are in the same combat as you
decisions.rest: her posse defends her

combat.taunt.what: a creature after her that one of her animals in her fight hits turns on that animal instead, with chance chance, for time seconds (a lunge at her already under way lands first; then it may come back to her).

decisions.quote: Taunt seems good

notice.what: Creatures notice her on the ground nearby: resting ones turn to look, curious babies come up to her.
notice.notes: Creatures notice the witch on the ground within radius metres (Ed's playtest: a larger responsive area makes them feel alive): resting ones turn to look at her; babies of a curious kind come up to about curious metres from her, skittish ones keep about skittish metres off (config/combat.json temperament).

dodge.what: Dodging matters: creatures commit to their strikes, so she can dodge them by moving or blinking away.

decisions.quote: almost all animals are easily evaded simply by walking backwards, even large swarms. Ideally good play should require effective use of dodge
decisions.rest: he picked all three

dodge.notes: Dodging matters [1]: against the witch only (fights between creatures as before). a, committed strikes: a creature closes on her at chase times its sprint (combat.pursuitRun, or its kind's pursuit: so a slow kind can still be outwalked), a melee one surges on at surge times its sprint while it winds up (no gliding to a stop), tracking her, aiming where she'll be when its blow arrives (her velocity times that time, times lead), until commit seconds before it lets go, when its aim locks (a blink then, or during its lunge, gets her clear), lunging lunge times its attack's lunge, its blow reaching width times its attack's range.

dodge.a.heavy.what: Heavy kinds chasing her build up speed and swing their charges toward her, so a burst or a blink gets clear.

decisions.quote: Maybe heavies can have a higher top speed, but slow acceleration?
shooters should have longer range

dodge.a.heavy.notes: chasing her, those species run at up to speed m/s (above her walk) built up at accel m/s each second, their charges swinging toward her at home degrees a second as they run, so a burst or a blink gets clear and a long retreat is run down (the snail, hedgehog and woodlouse left slow, the last two with their rolling charges; the mole with its own burrow); her blink keeps her untouchable for gone seconds (dash.gone otherwise); and at most tokens creatures wind up or strike at her at once (swarmTokens when swarm or more are on her), the rest keep their places. b, predictive aim: with ranged off (?ranged=old) the old pack bolts aim at release where she'll be when they arrive (times lead), their lobs where she'll be when they land (times lobLead); charges down the lane to where she'll be when they reach her (times chargeLead); a shot lives life times its range over its speed (1.3 before); the old pack bolt at her (a close kind's shot in a shooter's role, not a species' own) flies speed times as fast (chasing her at her walk it closes at only its speed less hers) and winds up at most windup seconds, lifted where ranged's lock needs it; a shot or lob at her reaches range times as far, the shooter keeping its usual distance [2]. A species' own shot takes neither speed nor windup: its speed is ranged.speedFloor's and its wind-up its own (Ed, 2026-11-12, option C: wind-ups as they were); With ranged on, every shot's and lob's lead is that rule's, followed through the wind-up, not taken at release. c, packs cut off her retreat: while she moves faster than moving times her walk, share of a pack of species (wolves, foxes, martens, bats) take places ahead of her (ahead seconds of her run on, angle radians either side of her heading, reach times their attack's reach out), sprinting at up to sprint m/s to get there. ?dodge=a,b,c turns on those named and off the rest (?dodge=0 none).

ranged.what: Creatures' shots aim where she's going: each follows her through its wind-up and locks a moment before it can reach her, so a steady walk gets hit and a change of direction dodges [1][2][3].

decisions.quote: creature ranged attacks (home island, mostly youths): the preparation time seems long, projectile speed is low, if you're moving at all they basically never hit you
decisions.rest: measured first (the ranged-hit harness, tools/balance/rangedhit.mjs): every species' shot aimed at where she stood as its wind-up started, so any steady movement took her out of its path

decisions.quote: when the changes are decided, apply them to all creatures, not just home ones

decisions.rest: lead plus a speed floor, with the report's sub-rules (bursts keep the first shot's lock, areas lock 0.7 s, homing, spirals, boomerangs and beams left out, walls half lead, the caster holding still from the lock, the old pack bolts taking the same lock); the three wrong things fixed in the same build (an adult's even fan with a hole in the middle, the young rhino's logs straddling her, dodge.b's speed and wind-up reaching only the old pack bolts); and the treetops kept untouchable

ranged.notes: Every ranged attack at her, every kind and level: its aim (the telegraph's lane or landing ring too) follows her through the wind-up at where she'll be when the shot arrives (lead times the way, her velocity as she goes), solving a curving or swaying path so it passes there; it locks at least commit s before the release and at least lock s (by level) before the shot can reach her; from the lock to the release the caster holds still, so the shot leaves from where it aimed. An area put down where she stands (and a mine or seed laid there) locks areaLock s ahead at every level; a wall of rollers leads rollerLead as far; a burst's, spray's or volley's later shots keep the first's locked aim. Straight bolts and rollers at her fly at least speedFloor times her ground speed (groundSpeed: 38.5 m/s at 19.25), an accelerating roller's profile scaled with it. Wind-ups as they were, lifted only where the lock couldn't otherwise hold (the old pack bolts' 0.35 s, dodge.b.windup). Left out of the lead and the floor: homing (owl, hydra), spirals, boomerangs, orbits, beams, melee, a pulse round itself, and pack interplay that goes by way of packmates (relay, tether, triangulate). Fans and walls always keep one body on the aim (an adult's even fan shifted half a step, a wall slid so the gap is beside her). The old pack bolts (a close kind's shot or lob in a shooter's role, rules/combat.ts) take the same lock and floor. The treetops unchanged: a witch off the ground can't be hit. ?ranged=old the old aim throughout.

ranged.on.what: on: shots aim where she's going (the ranged rule); off, as ?ranged=old: each aims at her place as its wind-up starts, the old pack bolts leading her as they let go, no speed floor, fans and walls as before.

ranged.lead.what: times the way to where she'll be when the shot arrives that the aim takes (1: all of it, 0: where she is), a wall of rollers rollerLead of it.

ranged.commit.what: seconds before its release that a shot's aim locks at the latest (the caster holds still from then).

ranged.lock.what: seconds before a shot can reach her that its aim locks at the latest, by the caster's level: a youth's longer, so a change of direction dodges it more often.
ranged.lock.notes: A per-level lead factor (babies lead less) measured as a cliff: at 0.85 every youth's shot fell to 0 to 8% across, so the level difference is made by when the aim locks instead (the measurement report, 2026-11-12).

ranged.speedFloor.what: a straight bolt or roller at her flies at least this many times her ground speed (2: 38.5 m/s at her 19.25).

ranged.areaLock.what: seconds before an area put down where she stands strikes (or a mine is laid there) that its aim locks, at every level: with no flight to see, the lock is all the warning she gets.

ranged.rollerLead.what: times the lead a wall of rollers takes (the rhino's and beaver's logs): a wall is wider than her change of direction, so at full lead it was the harshest attack.

shotMarks.what: Where a wild creature's shot ends without hitting (a bolt or roller that runs out, a lob landing), it leaves a small brief mark on the ground in its element that hurts or slows whoever of its foes stands in it [1].

quote: Enemy projectiles seem to have no effect where they land, is that correct?
decisions.rest: told that about 48 of 61 ranged kinds left nothing where a shot ended; he chose a brief mark in the shot's element that hurts or slows if you stand in it for a second or two

shotMarks.notes: Only a cast's own bolt, roller or lob marks the ground, and only one that leaves nothing of its own (a kind with its own zone or burst where it ends keeps that; the pieces of a burst leave none; her party's shots leave none). A mark is one of the attack engine's zones, drawn as they are in the shot's element and fading out. Her own health is counted in whole hits, so a hurting mark costs her one hit, at most once a mark, and only after she has stood in it for stand seconds running: walking through never costs it. Other animals: the shot's foes only, as every zone.

shotMarks.on.what: on: wild shots mark the ground where they end; off, as ?shotmarks=0: they leave nothing, as before.

shotMarks.time.what: seconds a mark lasts (a shot ending on a mark of its own side renews it instead of adding one).

shotMarks.radius.what: a mark's radius in metres (about her own width to twice it across).

shotMarks.stand.what: seconds running a foe must stand in a hurting mark before it bites, once a mark each.

shotMarks.damage.what: a hurting mark's bite on an animal, times what the shot's hit would have done (her: one hit whatever this is, unless it is 0).

shotMarks.slow.what: times her own speed while she stands in a slowing mark (frost, a puddle, a dark pool; an animal is slowed as by any slow).

shotMarks.rough.what: times her own speed on rough ground (earth, sand, wood, wind and bloom marks).

shotMarks.max.what: at most this many marks at once: a shot ending while there are this many leaves none (a big pack's volleys can't fill the zones).

shotMarks.merge.what: a shot ending within this many metres of a mark of its own side renews that mark rather than laying another.

shotMarks.kinds.what: what each element's mark does: hurt (stood in, it bites once), slow, rough (a milder slow) or none; a shot whose own hit slows or burns leaves a slowing or a hurting mark whatever its element.

stoneIdle.what: A wild area's hostile creatures gather and roam near its runestone.

decisions.quote: if you enter a hostile area and the animals are at the very opposite end, it can be quite a long time before they reach you, and so it feels like nothing is happening. I think we can solve this by having the hostile creatures tend to idle near the runestone

stoneIdle.notes: Hostile creatures gather near the runestone [1]: a wild area's own hostile young and adults (not its babies, its legend or its circle's baby, nor a friendly area's, nor happy, leashed or enraged ones) start, roam and nap anywhere in a disc of radius metres round its runestone, evenly spread (a loose cluster, not a ring), keeping clear metres off the stone itself; still inside their own area. Arriving at the stone means meeting them.

stoneIdle.on.what: false lets them roam the whole area as before.

sigilAvoid.what: Idling and dancing creatures keep off the sigils lying on the floor.

decisions.quote: When idling or dancing, creatures should try and avoid standing on floor sigils

sigilAvoid.notes: Creatures keep off floor sigils [1]: wild idlers, happy ones at their area, dancers and parked ones roaming round their sigil choose where to stand next off every sigil on the floor (her placed sigils, happy creatures' runes, relics' sigils, her hats lying down), and one resting on a sigil moves on. Only a nudge: with nowhere clear in a dozen tries it stands where it would have; moving, chasing, fighting and marching are untouched.

sigilAvoid.on.what: false lets them stand on sigils as before.

sigilAvoid.pad.what: Metres past a sigil's edge a creature's middle still counts as on it.

wildWatch.what: On her landing anywhere on the ground in a wild area (flying over starts nothing) its creatures stare and redden for a few seconds before they attack; walking out or taking off in that time calls it off.

decisions.quote: stir, evade and hang back, turning to LOOK at her
decisions.rest: when she enters a dormant area its animals nap, then, then attack; every creature looks, no special art

decisions.quote: make the dormant-to-attacking choreography slower, with a visible sign of aggro (e.g. red tint) rising that lets a player who wanders into a dangerous area understand what's happening and have time to run away
Six second dormant period should be four seconds
decisions.rest: 5.5 before, 2 before that

decisions.quote: remove the wild area aggro red glow
decisions.rest: the screen edges' red that went with it is gone

decisions.quote: should fade out rather than cut out instantly
decisions.rest: Initially 0.7 seconds; increased to 1.5 seconds by Ed on 2026-10-31 (coordinator brief #1476 comment 6549034570: the wild watch red should fade out more slowly).

decisions.quote: Animals should chase outside, and relatively far. The idea is to stop people just sitting near the edge of a territory and sniping/kiting. However if you leave the area before the warning ends then they don't attack

wildWatch.notes: The wild watch [1]: on a witch's first coming down on the ground in a wild area (not partified, not friendly, not home), its wild young and adults (not legends, the enraged or besiegers; babies keep their notice) hold off for time seconds, standing and turning to stare at her, any within hangBack metres backing off a little; then they fight as ever. The area is forgotten forget seconds after the last witch was on the ground in it, so a later visit plays it again. Slower, with a warning [2]: time is 4 s [3]; leaving the area or rising before it is up calls it off (they settle back and don't chase; the next visit starts it over). Over the watch each watcher reddens, from faint as they notice her to full just before they attack, the whole area together: its red up to tint [4], times the area's danger, its watchers' fighting value over dangerF (F, rules/power.ts) capped at 1, so a deep, crowded area reads as worse than a first-ring one. When the watch ends (they attack, she invites one, she leaves or rises) the red eases out over fade seconds (1.5, Ed 2026-10-31; previously 0.7) [5]. The chase [6]: leave before the warning's up and none comes after her; once they've attacked (the warning over with her inside) they follow her anywhere on the ground until she takes off (Ed's 31 Oct playtest; before, out to combat.leaveArea metres past their edge); and a 💌 of hers landing on a wild creature provokes it for provoked seconds: it comes out after her across its edge and on in the same way (no sniping from just outside).

wildWatch.on.what: false: they attack at once, as before.

wildWatch.inviteWakes.what: a 💌 landing on one of a wild area's creatures wakes the area at once: its watch is over (or never starts), and its own young and adults, napping or not, wake with no getting up and go for her at once, by the hunt's rules (rules/inviteWakes.ts); its babies, legend and circle baby as before.

hunt.what: Once the wild watch is over, every awake young and adult in the area hunts her while she's in it.

decisions.quote: When I go to a wild area, after they are awoken all of the wild creatures from that area should fight with me until either I die or they are invited. When they are all invited, the runestone transforms into a soundsystem. The legend and the circle baby are the exceptions
they should lose interest and go home if you leave their area, as they did before
decisions.rest: and; rules/hunt.ts

hunt.notes: The hunt [1][2]: once a wild area's watch is over with her on the ground in it, every one of its own awake young and adults hunts her while she's in the area, wherever in it they are, never giving up or napping; over the treetops there they hold and come on again when she lands. It ends for one when it's invited, enraged, or knocked down and run off; for all of an area's when she takes off outside the area (Ed's 31 Oct playtest: they follow her out on foot and hold while she's up over their own area; before, it ended as she left the area and they gave up combat.leaveArea metres past their edge); for all of hers when she's knocked out (they give up, walk home and roam, DECISION FOR ED, and the area's watch plays again on her next visit). Back in an area she left, it hunts her again at once while it's remembered (wildWatch.forget seconds after she was last on the ground in it), else its watch plays again. Babies don't fight.

hunt.on.what: false: the old rule (only those near her attack).

naps.what: Wild creatures roaming their area now and then lie down for a nap.

decisions.quote: I think animals in wild areas which are idling can sleep. They awake when you are there in ground mode, but stay asleep if you're in treetop mode, or not in their area (e.g. you see them from an adjacent area)
They don't all sleep - but it's one of the things they can do while idling

naps.notes: Wild idlers nap [1][2]: a wild creature roaming its own still-wild area (not besieging, fleeing, dazed, marching, fighting, happy or a legend), at each pause, lies down instead with chance, for length seconds (a range: min, max), then gets up. It gets up at once when a witch is on the ground in its area (none starts a nap then), and when its area is partified or it's enraged or taken; getting up takes wake seconds (a stretch, a yawn), out of fights till then, so landing isn't an instant pounce. Asleep it stays down with her in the treetops or on the ground in another area, however near. Sleepers skip their roam and every fight.

naps.circle.what: a legend circle's baby [1] naps at each pause with its own chance, for its own length (seconds), and is woken only by a witch on the ground within reach metres of its circle's edge (so she can still invite it), not anywhere in its area.

decisions.quote: the legend circle baby should spend most of its time napping when in the circle

guard.what: Creatures parked at a sigil on the ground guard it, fighting any wild creature that comes near.

decisions.quote: Animals leashed inside the home area should aggro enemy creatures within that area
Placing a sigil in any area should work as home does: the creatures defend the whole area, plus a radius round the sigil
A parked creature should guard its chain length, now that's a fixed number, with home area an exception
Animals parked in the home area can roam it freely.

guard.notes: Parked party animals (at a sigil on the ground) guard it [1]: they take on any wild creature of another kind near the sigil, and come back to it. One parked with its sigil in the home area (the dancefloor's) guards all of that area instead [2]: any wild or enraged creature anywhere in it, never one outside it; and it isn't held by its sigil there: it roams the whole home area freely [5] (rules/leash.ts roamHome); radius (40 m) is left only for a map with no home area or no chains. Parked in any other area [3], it guards all of its sigil's area and its chain's length round the sigil besides [4]: leash.chain.length (80 m), derived from it, not radius (rules/combat.ts guardRadius; with no chains, radius).

population.what: How many wild creatures each area starts with, more along the waves' route so the later areas are the dangerous ones.

decisions.rest: one baby and one young:, 'actually, the game should start with one baby and one youth, otherwise you can't avoid enraging lots of legends', after 'the game is hard! we should start each area with just one baby'; before it, one young and one adult, and before that one baby and two adults

decisions.quote: no population growth on a clock
decisions.rest: his new core design
the swarm plan's phase 1: its own young and adults, the ones a wave enrages and sets marching; rules/swarm.ts

a fraction carries over: 0.5 is one every other wave; balance: 0.5, from 1, so a player's defence can hold the early sieges and playing well matters (put to Ed; moot since his 2026-10-28 ruling below turned growth off)

decisions.quote: during a night, no creatures are created and none are destroyed
decisions.rest: growth.on off, so the balance simulators match the game; a creature that runs off sleeps on the beach (rules/runaway.ts)

population.notes: Wild creatures [1]: every area starts with the same population, population.start [2], and, from the start [3], more by its place on the waves' route (Balance 2's shape; rules/growth.ts routePopulation): byRoute's threat (since removed: the hostile swarm below does this now), [route index, F] points (1 the first wave's stone; straight lines between, flat past the ends), is the extra fighting value its young and adults add (F by Lanchester, young 11.6, adult 40, babies 0; about what an area woken at that wave grew to before); its kind spends it by its profile (byRoute's profiles by species (removed with it), else default: the shares of its extra creatures as babies, young and adults), so many more of a swarm's young than of a heavy kind's adults, at the same danger: count = threat ÷ the profile's mean F a creature × the area's count scale, rounded, split by the shares (largest remainder, ties by the seed). The hostile swarm [4]: its challenge grows with the area's place p in the runestone order (0 the first stone, 1 the last), whatever its species. Each area fields, of every size up to its species' cap (capScales: the cap grown along the same curve, at least 2) and every young/adult split, the one nearest the target; among those within swarm.mixTolerance (10%) of the nearest, a mix of young and adults first. A simulated power (config/swarm-power.json, empty in phase 1) stands in for the estimate where it has the swarm. So a default map (about 100 areas) holds about 540 hostiles: the curve's average, 5.8 an area. growth is the old growth on a clock, which the game no longer reads, off since [6] (the balance simulators read it only when on): every wave, each area the party hasn't reached gained growth.perWave more [5], each at a random level by growth.weights (baby, young, adult: equal thirds), so the areas the party reaches late are the ones to fear. Areas already partified don't grow. New ones arrive out of the witch's sight (beyond the haze's far edge plus growth.hide metres), never popping in on screen; areas far from every witch keep them as counts only, made real (from the seed) when a witch comes within creatureSimRadius of the area or it wakes. The home area holds none. Fighting value (DESIGN.md, Balance): a young is worth 15.5, an adult 29, a legend 76; so an area woken at wave n brings about 1 + n/3 young and 1 + n/3 adults (F about 44.5 + 14.8 n), besides its legend (wildLegends). Only creatures whose home is within creatureSimRadius metres of the witch move. node tools/balance/sim.mjs forecasts the sieges these numbers make.

population.byRoute.babies.what: babies in every area, start's included [1], at most babyCap.

decisions.rest: about two, for quest sigils and berries

population.byRoute.minHostile.what: at least this many young or adults in every wild area [1], any shortfall made up with young.

decisions.quote: every wild area has at least one hostile wild creature

population.swarm.classes.what: Swarm species come in strong, medium and light classes, smaller swarms of stronger creatures.
population.swarm.classes.notes: strong (cap 6), medium (cap 12: swarm.reference, and every species not listed) and light (cap 16; Ed: "a swarm of 20 is too many; cap it at 16"), each class's strength 12 / its cap on its creatures' health and damage (strong ×2, light ×0.75; rules/combat/data.ts), so moving a species is one line here. The target is the estimated power (Σhp × Σdps; the witch doesn't count: her three hits ignore damage) of a medium reference swarm of swarm.start + (swarm.endAverage − swarm.start)·p^swarm.curve creatures (1 + 11·p^0.8), its young share easing from swarm.youngShare[0] (1.0) to [1] (0.2). p is the area's place along its own island's route, (its place − 1)/(the route's length − 1), times its island's reach (its phase over swarm.fullPhase, at most 1; home's the share of the islands found: rules/swarm.ts islandShare, rules/growth.ts islandReach), so the last area of a phase 5 island fields the final swarm and an earlier phase's its share of the way along the curve.

population.swarm.fullPhase.what: the phase whose islands reach the full swarm at their last area; an island of an earlier phase its phase over this of the way along the curve.

decisions.quote: we should rebalance this so phase 5 islands get to full packs

population.swarm.fullPhase.notes: 5: a phase 5 island's last area fields the full swarm whatever its size, a phase 1 island's a fifth of the way (rules/swarm.ts phaseReach, rules/growth.ts islandReach). Home's reach is the share of the islands she's found (rules/rosters.ts foundShare: none at first, every island at the end); a map that's no island by roster plays the whole curve. It replaces the largest island's areas (largestIsland 50, 2026-11-03 to 11-04: an island's size over it, which only the 50-area phase 5 islands reached).

simLod.what: How far from her wild creatures are simulated every step; further off they're simulated coarsely, and past the sim radius not at all.

decisions.rest: creatures far from the action frozen until she comes closer; rules/simLod.ts

simLod.notes: The simulation's level of detail [1]. Wild creatures roaming are simulated every step within full.ground metres of the witch on the ground, full.treetop over the treetops (each a little past the most the view shows from there at any zoom: 178 and 262 m in a 1900 by 1240 window); beyond, coarsely: once every `every` steps (60 a second), by that many steps' time at once, taking turns; past creatureSimRadius not at all. Besiegers marching on a soundsystem are simulated every step within full of her or within action metres of a soundsystem, a party animal or a happy legend's guard; elsewhere coarsely, marching `every` steps at a time. Going out, one stays in full until band metres past the line, so none flickers. The debug overlay's sim line counts them.

creatureSpeeds.what: The witch is much faster than almost all creatures.
creatureSpeeds.notes: Ed [1]: the witch is much faster than almost all creatures (she flies at groundSpeed, 19.25 m/s, on the ground and treetopSpeed, 48, over the treetops; at first 14 and 32). Wild creatures amble at creatureSpeed m/s (legends legendSpeed); leashed ones run after their leash point at leash.runSpeed. The fast few (fast: hare, stoat, marten; rare, and weaker when combat comes) move fastMult times the usual; legends run at legend times it: very slow.
